name: Instagram Reels (organic) 9:16

house.codec: H.264 High, yuv420p, CRF 18, 2 B-frames, GOP 15
house.audio: AAC 48 kHz 320 kbps stereo; loudness per FD19
house.safe_box_px: x 65-1015, y 269-1248 (from Meta ads 14/35/6% rule, applied to organic as a house rule)

ffmpeg_command: ffmpeg -i master.mov -vf "fps=30,scale=1080:1920:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase:flags=lanczos,crop=1080:1920,scale=out_color_matrix=bt709:out_range=tv,format=yuv420p,setparams=color_primaries=bt709:color_trc=bt709:colorspace=bt709:range=tv" -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -profile:v high -g 15 -bf 2 -colorspace bt709 -color_primaries bt709 -color_trc bt709 -color_range tv -c:a aac -b:a 320k -ar 48000 -movflags +faststart reel.mp4
how: Render HTML/AI at 1080x1920 30 fps natively when possible; conform 24 fps AI clips (see spec.conform_24_to_30).
purpose: Accepted by Instagram above minimums, consistent colour on phones.
use_when: all IG Reels incl. carousel-to-Reel conversions
common_mistakes: 24 fps upload (below IG's stated 30 fps minimum)
bt709 tag without bt709 conversion (colour shift)
check: ffprobe: 1080x1920, 30/1, yuv420p, bt709 x3, tv; safebox PNG shows no text outside the box.
test_status: ffmpeg_command tested on testsrc2 (ffprobe verified tags) 2026-11-27

name: Meta (IG/FB) Reels ads 9:16
definition: Vertical ad creative for Reels placements.

official.safe_zone: top 14%, bottom 35%, sides 6% free of text/logos/key elements

ffmpeg_command: ffmpeg -i master.mov -vf "fps=30,scale=1440:2560:flags=lanczos,scale=out_color_matrix=bt709:out_range=tv,format=yuv420p,setparams=color_primaries=bt709:color_trc=bt709:colorspace=bt709:range=tv" -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 17 -profile:v high -c:a aac -b:a 320k -ar 48000 -movflags +faststart ad.mp4
how: Do not upscale 480x848 Wan output straight to 1440x2560 — upscale once with a good scaler, or deliver 1080x1920.
purpose: Meet ad spec; keep CTA visible.

official.note: No official organic Facebook Reels help page was opened this session; third-party guides disagree on minimums. Use the IG master.

name: TikTok 9:16
definition: Vertical master for TikTok (organic and in-feed ads).

official.ads_non_spark: 9:16 >= 540x960 (recommended orientation); mp4/mov/mpeg/3gp/avi; up to 10 min; <= 500 MB; bitrate >= 516 kbps
official.safe_zone: download TikTok's template (depends on caption length and add-ons such as anchors)

qc_command: overlay TikTok's downloaded safe-zone PNG: ffmpeg -i tiktok.mp4 -i tiktok_safezone.png -filter_complex overlay -frames:v 1 tmp/tt_safe.png
how: Keep right-hand icon column and bottom caption area free of text.
purpose: One 9:16 master that also passes TikTok ad minimums.

name: YouTube Shorts
definition: Square or vertical upload up to 3 minutes is categorised as a Short.

official.rule: square or vertical, <= 3 min (uploads on/after 15 Oct 2024)
official.content_id: Shorts > 1 min with active Content ID claim are blocked globally
official.encoding: YouTube upload settings: H.264 High, 2 B-frames, closed GOP half frame rate, VBR, 4:2:0, BT.709, AAC 48 kHz 384 kbps stereo; 1080p SDR 8 Mbps (24-30 fps), 12 Mbps (48-60 fps)

house.codec: H.264 High CRF 18 or VBR ~12 Mbps

ffmpeg_command: ffmpeg -i master.mov -vf "scale=1080:1920:flags=lanczos,scale=out_color_matrix=bt709:out_range=tv,format=yuv420p,setparams=color_primaries=bt709:color_trc=bt709:colorspace=bt709:range=tv" -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 18 -profile:v high -bf 2 -g 15 -c:a aac -b:a 384k -ar 48000 -movflags +faststart short.mp4
how: Upload at native frame rate (YouTube: encode at the recorded rate).
purpose: Be classified as a Short; meet YouTube encoding advice.
avoid_when: music with active claims and length > 60 s
common_mistakes: converting 24 fps to 30 for YouTube (not needed)

name: YouTube long-form 16:9 1080p SDR

official.container: MP4, no edit lists, moov at front
official.video: H.264 High, progressive, 2 B-frames, closed GOP = half frame rate, CABAC, VBR, 4:2:0
official.audio: AAC-LC or Opus, 48 kHz, 384 kbps stereo

house.fps: 24 for cinematic story clips, 30 for screen/UI

ffmpeg_command: ffmpeg -i master.mov -vf "scale=1920:1080:flags=lanczos,scale=out_color_matrix=bt709:out_range=tv,format=yuv420p,setparams=color_primaries=bt709:color_trc=bt709:colorspace=bt709:range=tv" -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 17 -profile:v high -bf 2 -g 12 -c:a aac -b:a 384k -ar 48000 -movflags +faststart yt.mp4
qc_command: ffprobe; watch on phone and laptop
how: Keep the timeline at the source frame rate.
common_mistakes: -g not matched to half frame rate (12 at 24 fps, 15 at 30)

name: YouTube 2160p SDR
definition: 4K upload for higher YouTube encode quality.

house.resolution: 3840x2160 only if source is >= 4K-quality; never upscale 480p AI clips to 4K

ffmpeg_command: ffmpeg -i master.mov -vf "scale=3840:2160:flags=lanczos,scale=out_color_matrix=bt709:out_range=tv,format=yuv420p,setparams=color_primaries=bt709:color_trc=bt709:colorspace=bt709:range=tv" -c:v libx264 -preset slow -b:v 40M -maxrate 45M -bufsize 80M -profile:v high -c:a aac -b:a 384k -ar 48000 -movflags +faststart yt4k.mp4
avoid_when: AI video sources (no real detail gain)

name: House mezzanine master (H.264 high quality)
definition: High-quality master from which all platform versions are made.

official.standard: BT.709 primaries/OETF; BT.1886 display gamma 2.4 reference; limited range 16-235 (8-bit) / 64-940 (10-bit)

house.codec: H.264 High CRF 14-16 or x264 10-bit if supported
house.colour: BT.709 converted with scale out_color_matrix + setparams tags

ffmpeg_command: ffmpeg -i render.mov -vf "scale=out_color_matrix=bt709:out_range=tv,format=yuv420p,setparams=color_primaries=bt709:color_trc=bt709:colorspace=bt709:range=tv" -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 15 -profile:v high -c:a aac -b:a 320k master.mp4
how: Grade on the master; platform versions only rescale/re-encode.
common_mistakes: default ffmpeg RGB->YUV uses BT.601 matrix (tested: pure red -> Y81/Cb90 default vs Y62/Cb102 with bt709)
check: ffprobe shows bt709 for space, primaries, transfer.
test_status: tested 2026-11-27 (matrix + tag behaviour of ffmpeg 9.0 verified)

name: ProRes 4444 with alpha (overlay interchange)
definition: Intermediate for transparent layers (glasses cutout animations, titles) between tools.

official.prores_4444: ~330 Mbps at 1080p29.97, 4:4:4:4 with alpha up to 16-bit

name: Conform 24 fps AI clips to a 30 fps timeline
definition: Wan 2.2 TI2V-5B (and our tools/wan.py) output 24 fps; Reels need >= 30 fps.

official.wan: TI2V-5B generates 720P at 24 fps (model card); wan.py encodes at 24 fps

house.option_A: fps=30 (frame repeat, 2 of every 4 frames doubled -> slight judder; safest, no artefacts)
house.option_B: minterpolate=fps=30:mi_mode=mci:mc_mode=aobmc (smooth but can warp edges/hands; check every shot)
house.option_C: build the whole timeline at 24 for YouTube and only conform the final Reel
house.option_D: setpts=0.8*PTS then fps=30 (speeds up 25%; only for ambient b-roll)

qc_command: step frame-by-frame through a pan; look for doubled frames (A) or warping (B)
how: Choose A for faces/products; B for slow nature/ambient.
purpose: Avoid 24 fps uploads to Reels and mixed-rate timelines.
use_when: any Wan/Kling clip in a 30 fps edit
common_mistakes: mixing 24 and 30 fps sources so cadence changes shot to shot
test_status: minterpolate and fps commands run on testsrc2 2026-11-27; visual quality untested

name: Synthetic 180-degree motion blur for HTML/rig animation
definition: Rendered HTML/puppet motion has zero blur (like a ~0 deg shutter) and can look stroboscopic on fast moves.

official.red: ~180 deg (1/48 s at 24 fps) is the cinema norm; smaller angles look stuttered, larger smeared

house.rule: exposure = (angle/360) x (1/fps); blur length ~ 50% of per-frame displacement for 180 deg look
house.implementation: render at 2-4x fps then average frames (tmix) before decimating, or CSS/GSAP directional blur on fast elements only

ffmpeg_command: ffmpeg -i render60.mp4 -vf "tmix=frames=2,fps=30" out30.mp4  (60 fps render, 2 samples 1/60 s apart per 1/30 s frame = ~180 deg; a 120 fps render with tmix=frames=3 approximates 240 deg — sample spacing x (frames-1) / frame duration x 360)
qc_command: pause on the fastest move: smear should be about half the gap between frames
how: Render at 60 fps, tmix 2 frames, output 30 fps = ~180 deg equivalent.
purpose: Filmic motion for kinetic type and puppets.
use_when: fast whip moves, falling objects, kinetic text
avoid_when: text that must be read during motion (keep crisp)
